name: Meta-Prompting
executive_summary: One LLM instance acts as a task-agnostic conductor: it decomposes a task, dispatches subtasks to fresh model instances (optionally with tool access), and synthesizes their outputs into a final answer.
description: A single high-level 'meta model' orchestrates the overall process without solving subtasks itself — it delegates each subtask to a fresh, appropriately-instructed instance, which may include using external tools, then integrates the returned results. Positioned as a task-agnostic generalization of the various chaining/agentic techniques, since the conductor's own prompt does not need task-specific tuning.
when_to_use: Complex, multi-part tasks spanning different subtask types (e.g. some needing computation, some needing retrieval) where a single fixed pipeline shape doesn't fit.
when_not_to_use: Simple or homogeneous tasks — the orchestration overhead isn't justified.
known_pitfalls: Conductor quality is a single point of failure for task decomposition, similar to Least-to-Most and Plan-and-Solve's dependency on their planning step.

primary_source.title: Meta-Prompting: Enhancing Language Models with Task-Agnostic Scaffolding
